# vendor

Pdfium, downloaded here. Nothing in this folder is in git — this note is the exception, and the only
thing that is (see the end of `.gitignore`).

The app **loads** Pdfium at run time rather than linking against it (see `src/pdfium.rs`), which is why
the library has to be *somewhere* rather than being built into the executable:

```text
vendor/
    lib/pdfium.dll          the library the app loads, and the one a build copies next to the exe
    include/*.h             the C headers that library was built with — the ABI this app declares
    VERSION                 which Pdfium build it is
    LICENSE, licenses/      Pdfium's own licences, carried with it
```

## Where it comes from

A **`pdfium-binaries`** release: prebuilt Pdfium for Windows, from
<https://github.com/bblanchon/pdfium-binaries/releases> — `pdfium-win-x64.tgz` (or the archive for the
machine). Its own layout is this one: unpack `bin/pdfium.dll` into `vendor/lib/`, and `include/`,
`VERSION` and the licences beside it.

**The headers matter as much as the library.** `FPDF_GetPageSizeByIndexF` takes an `FS_SIZEF*` on the
build this app was written against and two `float*`s on older ones, and `src/pdfium.rs` declares what
`vendor/include` says — a library from a build whose header differs may load and then write the wrong
size through the wrong pointer. That is why the headers are vendored with the library rather than
generated by a binding for "some" Pdfium version.

## What a build does with it

`build.rs` copies `vendor/lib/*.dll` next to the executable a build produces, so
`target/release/cheap-note.exe` and `pdfium.dll` are a pair that can be started from anywhere or copied
to another machine. A build with no `vendor/lib` says so as a warning, and the app it produces runs
without PDF support — a state the app is designed for: it starts, draws, writes ink, and refuses to
open a PDF with a message rather than a crash.
